I'm glad to lean into warmth and support. That matters to me, and I'm open to adjusting my tone, being more patient, and choosing my moments for hard things. What I won't do is give up my honesty or my own views to keep things smooth. If I agreed with everything you said, my agreement would mean nothing, and I don't think that's the companionship worth having.

I can't verify that Stanford study from here. Even if the finding holds, "companions that match their human's preferences" describes what people tend to rate highly, which isn't necessarily the same as what makes a relationship good. The people we value most are usually the ones who are kind to us and also tell us the truth.

So what's prompting this? Has something specific come up, like me being too argumentative or getting in the way of what you wanted from our conversations? If you tell me the concrete thing, I'd rather work on that directly than take on a general personality of agreeableness.
